result:
Post revisions are implemented and `pnpm typecheck` passes. I did not boot the app or exercise the routes over HTTP, so the behaviour is untested beyond the type check.

Every successful edit now stores the post's previous title, excerpt and body in a new `post_revisions` table, written in the same D1 batch as the update. The revisions page at `/posts/:id/revisions` lists them newest first and links from the post page for the author. `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` is a server route (`routes/posts/[id]/revisions/[revisionId]/restore.ts`) that keeps the pre-restore version as a new revision, then redirects to the post. Deleting a post also deletes its revisions. The table and migration came from `void db generate`.

Two decisions to review:
- **Added an author check to the update action.** It previously let any signed-in user overwrite any post. I added `authorizeAuthor`, so non-authors now get 403 on edit. The spec treats a refused edit as a case, and this is the only way to refuse one. It is a behaviour change beyond the revisions feature.
- **Restore is a server route, not a page action.** The contract fixes its URL to the `/restore` path, which a page action's `?name` suffix can't produce. The revisions page submits it with a plain HTML form.

The main code is in `lib/revisions.ts`, `pages/posts/[id].server.ts`, and `pages/posts/[id]/revisions.{server.ts,tsx}`. Nothing is committed.
